stage: Growth (scaling COD orders across tier-2/3 Vidarbha & Marathwada)
title: A Maharashtra agri-inputs brand cut COD RTO from 41% to 14% with Marathi WhatsApp routed through Krishi Mitra dealers
content: SITUATION: We sold bio-fertilizers and pesticides (AOV ₹1,800) to cotton and soybean farmers across tier-3 Vidarbha and Marathwada. Our Meta and Google ads ran in English/Hindi, pushed a form, and looked fine on paper at ₹320 CPL. The hidden leak: COD RTO sat at 41% and repeat rate under 8%. Farmers wouldn't pay cash to a faceless city brand they couldn't call in Marathi. ACTION: We killed English top-funnel ads and shot 40-second Marathi demo videos on an actual Akola farm, running them on YouTube and Meta within a 25-50km radius of 60 mandis. Every CTA was click-to-WhatsApp, never a form. We onboarded 35 local Krishi Mitra dealers as verified WhatsApp contacts and listed them on Justdial, so a farmer in Yavatmal chatted with a known village agent who confirmed crop-stage dosage and arranged COD. OUTCOME: Over 5 months CPL fell to ₹190, RTO dropped 41%→14%, WhatsApp-to-order conversion hit 22%, and repeat purchase climbed to 31% as dealers nudged next-cycle reorders. CAC fell 38%; monthly orders grew 600→2,400 on ₹9L spend.
lesson: In rural India the trusted local dealer is your landing page — not a form. When you can't manufacture brand trust at a distance, borrow it: route the last mile through a known village agent on vernacular WhatsApp, and RTO, COD risk and repeat rate fix themselves because a real person vouches for the order.
